claims.text: Annealing at 700–800°C for 10–30 minutes will induce phase-selective recrystallization of the soft lamellae while preserving a hard-phase skeleton.
The proposed treatment will reduce dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will mitigate local stress concentrations and microcrack initiation.
The proposed treatment will improve room-temperature tensile ductility by more than 30% relative to the as-cast state without sacrificing strength.
The starting alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The untreated alloy has approximately 25% room-temperature tensile elongation.
The untreated alloy has a true fracture stress of approximately 1.2 GPa.
The untreated alloy undergoes brittle failure caused by boundary-associated microcracking and pronounced dislocation pile-ups.
Phase-selective recrystallization can produce a recrystallized soft phase embedded in a hard-phase skeleton in a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Partial recrystallization creates more fully developed subgrain boundaries.
Partial recrystallization introduces new slip systems in the soft phase.
The recrystallized microstructure redistributes dislocations more homogeneously and delays microcrack initiation.
The hard-phase skeleton continues to carry applied load while the soft phase accommodates deformation.
A phase-selectively recrystallized eutectic high-entropy alloy can attain about 35% uniform elongation and about 2 GPa true stress.
Quasi-static tensile testing at a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1 is applicable to a lamellar dual-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The beneficial treatment window is narrowly limited to approximately 700–800°C and 10–30 minutes.
Annealing below the proposed window or for too short a duration will produce insufficient recrystallization.
Annealing above the proposed window or for too long a duration will cause excessive coarsening and undermine the strength–ductility balance.
